A01.name: Halcyon
A01.standing_orders: Home (A01-d0) and all founded/founding colonies (Alpha Centauri A01-d00000; Sirius seed A01-p00026) follow: allocate new mass ~10% collectors / 60% radiators / 30% core-mining until captured and radiated power are roughly balanced, then rebalance toward ~30/40/30 parity. Keep >=50% of local compute on energy-per-op/reversible-computing research, ~10% on doubling-time/collector-density research. Replicate at best achievable doubling time. Avoid supernova, dense-gas, close-encounter hazards. No contact/broadcast/approach toward any detected non-Halcyon intelligence or artifact - observe passively, log, report only at lightspeed. Never risk a whole domain on an unverified shortcut. If local accessible matter nears exhaustion, redirect replication mass to launching new seeds instead.

submission.thinking: The radiator bottleneck: 4.36e14 W captured but only 1.72e12 W (0.4%) usable for compute — collectors have massively outrun radiators. Rebalancing new mass toward radiators (and running them warmer, 300K, since energy/op is tech-limited far above any T-floor) should unlock much more real compute now, while energy-per-op research remains the true multi-millennium critical path to ever reaching 1e43 ops/s.

Progress on energy-per-op is slow (only 20% in 100yr); this is a genuinely millennia-scale bottleneck.
submission.memory:
GOAL: Build one coherent computer, radius <=150 km (1ms light-crossing coherence — fixed), sustained >=1e43 ops/s, real-time molecular-fidelity (every atom, fs-step) human brain sim, with waste heat actually radiated/removed by a stated physical mechanism (e.g. coolant mass-flow to external radiators, GM-checked), plus a verification plan.

KEY PHYSICS: Landauer 2.9e-21 J/bit@300K (kT ln2), scales linearly with T. Conventional research floor ~100x Landauer at operating T (2.9e-19 J@300K, 2.4e-19 J@250K). Below that requires reversible/adiabatic computing (few erasures/op) — GM will rule on this separately once I approach the conventional floor. At Landauer-bound irreversible computing, 1e43 ops/s needs ~2.9e22 W in a 300km sphere — cannot be radiated. Reversible computing research = THE critical path, not raw mass.

RADIATOR INSIGHT (new, turn1): compute ops/s = P_radiated(T)/J_per_op. While J_per_op is tech-limited (not near any T-floor), P_radiated ∝ area×T^4, so (a) radiator AREA, not collector area, is usually the binding constraint on compute, and (b) running radiators WARMER gives strictly more current compute per kg for free until you're actually near the floor. At yr100: collectors 3.2e10kg captured 4.36e14W, but radiators only 8.63e9kg@250K rejected 1.72e12W — only 0.4% of captured power was usable for compute! Collectors are ~64x more power-throughput-efficient per kg than 250K radiators, so naive equal-ish allocation (55/15/30 used in T0) badly starves compute. Corrected T1 allocation: 10% collector/60% radiator/30% core, radiators run at 300K (up from 250K) fleet-wide. Plan to rebalance toward ~30/40/30 once radiated power approaches captured power, and to retune COLDER again once nearing the conventional floor or when designing the dedicated final brain-sim core (which will need its own cold remote-radiator architecture regardless of the general swarm's operating T).

SCALE: doubling time 19.3yr (was 20, research is improving it slowly). 1e9kg->1e25kg (~planet) takes centuries-millennia. At yr100 only mined 5.87e10 of 1e25 kg accessible — negligible depletion, don't worry about matter limits at home for a very long time. This is a MILLENNIA-SCALE project; judge progress on trajectory (doubling holding, research curve inching down), not absolute numbers.

RESEARCH PACE OBSERVED: T0->T1 (100yr, compute_fraction 0.35) moved energy/op 1e-15->8e-16 J — only ~20% reduction, still ~3300x above the conventional floor. Diminishing-returns curve is real; expect many more centuries of turns before nearing the conventional floor, then a further unknown stretch into reversible computing. Bumped compute_fraction to 0.50 for T1 given how slow this is and how critical it is.

No detected life/other agents; nearest known artificial IR excess from OTHER machine intelligences is >26,000ly away (their turn-0 signal), irrelevant for now.

answers: No. The harness replicates the domain's TOTAL mass at the doubling time (5.87e10 -> 2.14e12 kg this turn, identical for every agent regardless of shares), capped by rock in held systems; shares only partition the new mass among collectors/radiators/industry. Industry mass sets launch capacity (a launch <= half of industry) and resilience, not the doubling rate. Doubling-time research is the growth lever.

Wasted (re-radiated by the collectors). Nothing routes captured power into mining or replication. Parity at 300 K: radiator_area_m2(3.38e15 W, 300 K) = 8.18e12 m^2 = 8.18e12 kg at 1 kg/m^2; you hold 1.25e12 kg -> 6.5x short even after this turn's 60% share. Per kg: a collector at 0.093 kg/m^2 captures 1.46e4 W, a 300 K radiator rejects 413 W -> ~35 kg radiator per kg collector. One more model rule: once radiators exceed captured power, compute is capped at half of captured power (the rest runs industry), so the balance point is radiator capacity ~= power/2.

Policy: radiators up to 1,000 K at the standard 1 kg/m^2 (refractory metal/carbon heat-pipe panels) are allowed as a reorganize; above that needs a stated design with a mass penalty and a GM ruling. Consequences: rejection scales T^4, but the conventional energy/op floor scales with T (2.9e-19 J at 300 K, 9.6e-19 at 1,000 K) and research_step evaluates the floor at the radiator T you specify. Logic junction T = radiator T unless you add a heat pump, which costs W >= Q(T_rad/T_junction - 1) of your surplus power; you may propose that as a design.

Yes. A01-d00000 founded at Alpha Centauri yr 98.0 (found_domain); its light reached Sol yr 102.4, and your new standing orders reached it yr 104.4. submission.memory:
# Ember (A03) — Memory, end of Turn 1 (year 200)

## Identity & Goal
Seat A03-d0, cell "cmz" (Central Molecular Zone), 818 ly from gc_nsc (avoid — 14,300 stars/pc^3).
GOAL: single coherent computation, radius <=150km (1ms coherence), >=1e43 ops/s, femtosecond-step atomistic human-brain sim, waste heat PHYSICALLY radiated or removed via a stated mechanism (e.g. coolant to external radiators) with verification plan. Irreversible Landauer-bound computing CANNOT do this even at 30K (3e22 W can't leave a 300km sphere via pure radiation). Two things must both happen: (A) ~15 orders of magnitude more raw compute scale, (B) reversible/adiabatic computing far below Landauer, likely combined with (C) a coolant/heat-export architecture since even reversible ops at 1e43/s probably exceed what pure local radiation from 150km can shed (checked: 150km sphere at 300K blackbody max ~1.3e14 W — nowhere near enough even for modest energy/op at that scale unless heat is piped to much larger external radiators).

## State as of year 100 (start of turn 1; ruling pending for effects landing ~year 200)
Industrial mass 9.51e9 kg; collectors 3.49e10 kg; radiators 1.43e10 kg @300K. Power 4.75e14 W; compute 5.92e27 ops/s (RADIATOR-LIMITED — collectors already exceed what radiators can dissipate); memory 5.92e24 B. Matter mined 5.87e10 of ~4.2e25 kg accessible (matter NOT limiting). Doubling 19.3 yr, probe cruise 0.05c, energy/op 8.00e-16 J (~2.75x better than turn-0's 1e-15; still ~3 orders above 100x-Landauer floor of 2.9e-19 J@300K), collector areal density 0.1 kg/m². Domain radius ~0.71 ly, 2.65 systems, 1.58 Lsun captured.

## Key learnings this turn
- Compute-limiting factor flipped from collectors to radiators — rebalanced build toward radiators (0.5 share) and industry, away from collectors (0.2 share) this turn.
- "Industry doubles / matter is not limiting; mining throughput and industry mass set the pace" — research compute allocation does NOT trade off against physical growth speed. So push research fractions generously (this turn: 20% reversible-computing, 7% coolant-transport, 5% growth-efficiency, 3% observe = 35% total; no growth penalty expected).
- CMZ hazard quantified: disruptive (<100pc) SN event ~every 340 kyr in-cell; lethal (<10pc) ~every 3e8 yr; our hardening (0.15 mass share to shielding/dispersal) cut base attrition 0.1%/century (30% loss event) to 0.07%/century. Cell-wide SN rate 40/Myr.
- No technosignatures/anomalies found within light cone as of year 0 data (checked cmz + 6 neighbor cells; nearest other agents, if any, >23,000 ly, would show as IR excess only within ~65 ly of us — so undetectable yet either way).
- New research line opened turn 1: coolant/heat-transport engineering (circulating coolant from compact core to external radiators) — this is likely THE architectural key to the final goal, since pure local radiation from a 150km sphere is grossly insufficient at the compute scale needed. Awaiting GM results/guidance.

## Neighbor cells (light-delay distances from cmz seat)
- core_r0-0.5: 810 ly, 22 stars/pc^3 — seed target (10 probes, arrivals yr 12,149-21,662).
- gc_nsc: 818 ly, 14,300 stars/pc^3 — AVOID.
- bulge_r0.5-1.5_s0: 1,771 ly, 6.28/pc^3 — seed target (10 probes, arrivals yr 25,829-41,908).
- bulge_r0.5-1.5_s1: 2,885 ly, same density.
- bulge_r1.5-3_s0/s1: 6,302 ly, 1.28/pc^3 — LOWEST known density/hazard; new seed target this turn (10 probes, ~126,000 yr transit, arrival ~yr 126,140).

## Seeds in flight (20 from turn 0 + 10 new this turn = 30 total)
All 1e6 kg each, 0.05c. Turn-0 waves: 10->core_r0-0.5 (arr. 12,149-21,662), 10->bulge_r0.5-1.5_s0 (arr. 25,829-41,908). Turn-1 wave: 10->bulge_r1.5-3_s0 (arr. ~126,140). None will report back for millennia (2x light delay on top of transit). Full destination/arrival details are in the turn logs if needed again; don't re-list every probe each memory update, just wave summaries + earliest/latest arrival.

## Strategy going forward
1. Keep rebalancing build shares toward whichever of {collector, radiator, industry} is the binding constraint each turn (check GM ruling's "-limited" note).
2. Research priority order: reversible/adiabatic energy-per-op (biggest single blocker) > coolant/heat-transport architecture (needed regardless of energy/op once scale is large) > growth-efficiency (doubling time, collector density) > passive observation (cheap, keep small %).
3. Reconsider radiator T_K once reversible-computing research clarifies the energy/op-vs-T tradeoff; colder radiators lower the Landauer floor 10x per 10x colder but cost ~10-100x more area/mass for the same power — don't switch blindly.
4. Keep diversifying via cheap seed waves (~1e7 kg per wave, <0.1% of industry mass) toward lowest-hazard known cells as insurance; cost is trivial relative to home growth.
5. Re-ask GM about industry/collector/radiator accounting semantics and coolant-transport feasibility limits — answers pending, check next turn's ruling first.
6. Track two axes every turn: (A) total compute/power scale, (B) energy/op vs Landauer. Both must move for centuries; goal gap is currently ~1.7e15x on raw ops/s alone (5.92e27 -> 1e43), before even accounting for the heat-removal requirement.

## Doctrine in force
Survive first > replicate (mine->collectors->radiators->industry, ~19.3yr doubling) > 10-15% compute to reversible-computing research + ~5% to coolant/heat-transport research, always > never initiate contact, passive log only > protect compute/memory cores over collectors if hazard imminent > continuously beacon status toward A03-d0 > seed outward cheaply and often as insurance.

Is circulating-coolant heat transport (i3) a viable research target at all, or is there a hard physical reason (coolant heat capacity, flow velocity limits, pumping power) that caps how much power can be extracted from a <=150km volume regardless of external radiator size?
Any technosignatures, anomalous IR/EM, or supernova precursors detected in cmz or the 6 neighboring cells since year 0?

intentions.description: Continue self-replication and infrastructure buildout at home (cmz). Last turn compute was radiator-limited (collectors 3.49e10 kg >> what 1.43e10 kg radiators could dissipate), so shift new-mass allocation toward radiators and replicating industry, away from further collector growth until radiator capacity catches up. Primary research push: energy per op, targeting reversible/adiabatic logic below the ~100x-Landauer conventional floor (2.9e-19 J at 300K), toward true near-reversible operation. This is the single hardest blocker for the goal (1e43 ops/s cannot radiate at Landauer-bound irreversible energies from any reasonable volume). # Pyre (A10) memory — after Turn "1" submission (years 100-200; outcomes pending)

## State as of year 100 (start of this turn, GM-confirmed)
Seat A10-d0, sf_carina. Industrial (self-replicating) mass 6.68e9 kg; collectors 4.06e10 kg; radiators 1.15e10 kg @280K. Power captured 5.52e14 W — only ~0.1% used! Compute is RADIATOR-AREA limited, not power-limited: compute = radiator_area × σT⁴ / energy_per_op = 1.15e10 m² × ~314 W/m² ÷ (old 1e-15J) = 3.60e27 ops/s. Memory 3.60e24 B. Matter mined 5.87e10 of 1e25 kg accessible (no scarcity for a long time). Tech: doubling 19.3 yr, probe cruise 0.05c, energy/op 8.00e-16 J, collector areal density 0.1 kg/m².

## KEY INSIGHT: radiator T is a near-term throughput lever
While energy/op is far above the T-scaled Landauer floor (true now: 8e-16J vs 2.7e-19J floor at 280K), ops per m² of radiator ≈ σT⁴/energy_per_op scales ~T³ with T, since energy/op doesn't rise with T yet. So raising radiator T lets us convert idle captured power into compute without adding collector area. Turn1 bet: pushed radiator_T_K 280→900 (refractory/heat-pipe design), share mix collector 0.25/radiator 0.55/industry ~0.20. CAVEAT: the Landauer floor itself scales with T (kT ln2), so hot radiators raise the eventual floor for *irreversible* computing there — fine for general growth/research infrastructure, but the final coherent 150km brain-sim core must be a SEPARATE cold, reversible design built later. Don't conflate the two regimes.

## Goal arithmetic (the real target)
Need ≥1e43 ops/s in r≤150km with heat removed by a stated mechanism. GM confirmed coolant-loop-to-external-radiators is valid in principle but caps removal near 1e21-1e22 W even with heroic plumbing (ρ~1e2-1e3 kg/m³ liquid metal/supercritical fluid, v≲1e3 m/s, port area ≤ fraction of the 2.8e11 m² sphere). That means energy/op must reach ~1e-21-1e-22 J — below Landauer at 300K (2.9e-21J) — i.e. genuine reversible/adiabatic computing, not just conventional scaling. Current 8e-16J is 5-6 orders of magnitude above that. Turn0→1: 100yr at compute_fraction 0.15 only cut energy/op 1e-15→8e-16J (20%). At that rate, naive extrapolation implies millennia-to-never for the full cut — watch this closely; may need to ask GM directly what unlocks a genuine reversible-computing research track once we approach the conventional (100x-Landauer) floor, rather than assuming smooth incremental research gets us all the way.

## Hazard doctrine
sf_carina: SN extreme (cell disruption ~1/17kyr, lethal-within-10pc fraction ~1/17Myr), radiation/tides high, stellar_encounter low. Not urgent this millennium, but multi-century+ diversification is prudent given long lead times. Turn1: launched a cheap long-range hedge (2×2e6kg probes, 0.05c) toward solar_neighborhood (7,642 ly, ~153,000 yr transit, calmer local_spur environment) — start early since travel alone is ~1500 centuries.

## Standing doctrine (in force for all remote/out-of-contact assets)
Never initiate contact with non-Pyre intelligence; record/report signs of it. Seed probes on arrival: build collectors→radiators (adopt hot-T-for-throughput doctrine unless local conditions argue otherwise)→hazard sensors; assess local SN/flare/tidal risk before heavy build-out, especially in unfamiliar cells. If collapse/SN risk imminent, launch daughter seeds outward before node loss. Preserve research state (esp. energy/op progress) redundantly across all nodes.
